issues.description: The problem statement specifies checkOrderReady() as returning void (UML and textual description), but the provided solution implementation declares public boolean checkOrderReady() and returns a boolean. This return-type mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about the expected method signature and whether they should return a value.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's checkOrderReady method signature match the problem specification by changing it to public void checkOrderReady() and remove the boolean return value (adjust internal logic accordingly), or alternatively update the problem statement and UML to indicate that checkOrderReady() returns boolean. Ensure the template and tests (if any) use the same signature.
